q: How do I start my video in an old 4:3 frame and then open it up to full widescreen?
a: 1. Apply Crop to the clip (Effects ▸ Legacy ▸ Video Effects) with Left and Right at 12.5 % each, which leaves a 4:3 window in a 16:9 frame. 2. At the reveal, keyframe Left and Right back to 0 % over about a second (`effects.toggleAnimation`), eased so it settles. 3. Time it to a beat or a line so the opening feels motivated. With several clips under it, put the same Crop keyframes on each, or nest them first (`clip.nest`) and crop the nest.

q: aspect ratio reveal but with the old part looking old too
a: Before the reveal, grade the clip faded and grainy (lifted blacks, less saturation, grain on the last node); at the reveal cut to, or dissolve into, the clean grade. A copy of the clip with the old look above it whose Opacity fades out (`effects.toggleAnimation`) does the change in one move.

q: Go from vertical phone framing to full widescreen in one move.
a: Crop Left and Right keyframed from a 9:16 window (about 34 % each side in a 16:9 frame) to 0 %, eased; the subject must sit in the middle of the frame for the narrow start to work.

q: How do I put my title over a blurred version of the shot so the text reads clearly?
a: 1. Apply Gaussian Blur to the shot under the title (`effects.apply`), Blurriness up and Repeat Edge Pixels on so the edges don't go dark. 2. Keyframe Blurriness so the shot blurs as the title comes in and clears as it leaves (`effects.toggleAnimation`). 3. Darken it a little with a Color Matte or the grade so the text has contrast. 4. The title on the track above (`graphics.newText`).

q: only the area behind the text should blur not the whole shot
a: Blur a copy of the shot on the track above it and limit that copy with a mask around the title area on Opacity (`masks.add`), with Mask Feather so the edge is soft; or use a box shape behind the text instead.

q: Same blurred-background look under every chapter title.
a: Put an Adjustment Layer (`file.newAdjustmentLayer`) under the title track with the Gaussian Blur keyframes on it, and save that blur as an effect preset (`presets.save`) to drop on the next chapter's adjustment layer.

q: How do I give each part of a music video its own colour look: cold verses, warm chorus?
a: 1. Markers at each section of the song (`markers.add`). 2. An Adjustment Layer (`file.newAdjustmentLayer`) over each section with Lumetri on it: the verse look cool and muted, the chorus warm and saturated. 3. Short dissolves or a cut on the beat between the adjustment layers. 4. Balance the clips themselves first so the looks sit on a neutral base.

q: look on the adjustment layer is fighting each clip's grade
a: An adjustment layer's grade sits after each clip's own nodes: keep the clips' grades to balance only, and put the creative look on the adjustment layer; for a per-camera fix append the same node to those clips (`grade.append`).

q: Swap the chorus look onto a different section later without regrading.
a: Move or copy the adjustment layer (it carries the look) to the new section, or copy a clip's grade and paste it (`grade.copy`, `grade.paste`) where the look belongs to the clips themselves.

q: How do I make a glowing neon sign title that flickers on?
a: 1. A text layer (`graphics.newText`) in a bright pink or cyan on a dark shot. 2. Edge Glow or Wonder Glow on the title clip for the tube glow (`effects.apply`). 3. Keyframe Opacity on and off a few times with Hold interpolation (`effects.setInterpolation`) for the flicker, then leave it on. 4. A buzz sound typed SFX under the flicker.

q: neon title should light up the wall behind it
a: On the shot's grade, a soft window around the title area with Gain pushed towards the neon colour, its strength keyframed to flicker with the title.

q: Neon title colours look dull after export.
a: Pick colours that hold up in Rec. 709 and check them after the grade; extremely saturated colours clip, so slightly less saturation with more glow reads brighter.

q: How do I turn a two-hour drawing recording into a 60-second speed-art video?
a: 1. Speed / Duration (`clip.speedDuration`) to the length you want (about 12 000 % for 2 h → 60 s), or cut out the pauses first. 2. Time interpolation Frame Blending for a smoother look, or Frame Sampling for crisp strokes (`clip.setTimeInterpolation`). 3. Music over it, ending on the finished drawing held for a few seconds (`clip.frameHold`). 4. Stabilize first if the camera drifted.

q: speed art flickers because my hand keeps covering the drawing
a: Cut out the stretches where the hand covers most of the page before speeding up, or let it run with Frame Blending, which softens the hand into a blur.

q: Show the final drawing next to the timelapse at the end.
a: Hold the last frame (`clip.frameHold`) or use a photo of the finished piece, and put it beside the timelapse as a split screen or a picture-in-picture for the last seconds.

q: How do I build a story from a long interview by working with the transcript instead of scrubbing?
a: 1. Transcribe the sequence (`transcript.generate`). 2. Duplicate the sequence first so the full interview stays. 3. Read the Transcript tab, search key phrases (`transcript.search`), and remove what you don't want: select the words (`transcript.select`) and Extract (`transcript.extract`) closes the gap. 4. Reorder the remaining bites on the timeline, then cover the cuts with B-roll.

q: transcript edit leaves jumpy cuts in the middle of sentences
a: Trim each cut to a breath or a pause, add a short audio crossfade so it doesn't click, and cover visible jumps with B-roll or a punch-in.

q: Mark the best quotes in the transcript to come back to later.
a: Put a marker on each quote while reading (`markers.add` with a name), or extract each to a selects sequence; markers can be filtered by colour later.

q: How do I make whispered dialogue audible without the background getting loud too?
a: 1. Type the clip Dialogue (`essentialSound.setType`). 2. Reduce Noise and Voice Isolation first so the room doesn't come up with it. 3. Then raise the whisper: clip gain (`clip.audioGain`) and Dynamics (a compressor) to bring it up evenly. 4. Check against the louder lines so the whisper stays a little quieter, as it should.

q: whisper got louder but the s sounds are harsh now
a: Add DeEss in Essential Sound's Repair section (or a de-esser) after the gain and compression; boosting quiet speech brings up sibilance.

q: One whispered line in a scene of normal talking.
a: Raise just that clip with Volume keyframes or the Audio Clip Mixer (`clipMixer.set`) and leave the rest; set the dialogue level first and fit the whisper slightly under it.
